title: The feud of the two houses

plan.english: Two houses stood by the river. In the one house dwelt Of-Good-Fame; in the other dwelt Man-Minded. Of-Good-Fame stole a horse from Man-Minded and killed him. The son of Man-Minded grew up and killed Of-Good-Fame. Then the son of Of-Good-Fame killed him. The grandsons fought at the ford, and they fell. No one paid a price, and no one took one. Now grass grows on their hearths.

clauses.english: Two houses stood by the river.

Of-Good-Fame stole a horse from Man-Minded and killed him.
The son of Man-Minded grew up and killed Of-Good-Fame.
Then the son of Of-Good-Fame killed him.
The grandsons fought at the ford, and they fell.
No one paid a price, and no one took one.
Now grass grows on their hearths.

plan.english: A widow nourished her son. In the nights she said to him: Ill-Minded killed your father. The boy grew strong. She gave him his father's spear. He went to the house of Ill-Minded and killed him at his hearth. Then the sons of Ill-Minded came in the night and burned the widow's house. The widow and her son died in the fire. So vengeance devoured two houses.

plan.english: A herdsman swore an oath by Sky. He said: I will pay the blood-price at harvest. Harvest came, and he did not pay. By night he fled with his cattle. At the ford the water rose, and the river took him and his cattle. Sky had seen his lie. His sons did not find his body. Whoever breaks an oath, the gods do not forget him.

His sons did not find his body.
Whoever breaks an oath, the gods do not forget him.

title: The widow who drove back the cattle

plan.english: The slayer's kin led a hundred cows to the widow. She did not take them. She drove them back to the slayer's house. For seven years they led the cows to her, and she drove them back. Her son grew up at the hearth. Then she gave him a knife and said: Now bring me the price. He brought blood; he did not bring cattle.

title: The elder who judged his son

plan.english: The elder's son killed a guest at the feast. The guest's kin came to the assembly and asked for the price. The elder said to his son: Pay the price of the guest. The son said: I will not pay. Then the elder decided: Go away from our village. You are not my son. The son went away, and the elder paid the price with his own cattle. There was peace between the two houses.

plan.english: Whoever kills a free man, let him pay a hundred cows to the kin of the dead man. Whoever kills a woman, let him also pay a hundred cows. Whoever kills a child, let him pay twice. If the slayer does not pay, let the kin of the dead take his blood. If they take the price, let no one shed blood.

Whoever kills a child, let him pay twice.
If the slayer does not pay, let the kin of the dead take his blood.
If they take the price, let no one shed blood.

plan.english: If a man kills a kinsman at a feast, let no one seat him at his hearth. Let him not drink mead with the men. Let no one speak his name. If anyone kills a guest at a hearth, let the master of the house pay the guest's price, because he guards the guest. A guest is dear to the gods.

clauses.english: If a man kills a kinsman at a feast, let no one seat him at his hearth.
Let him not drink mead with the men.
Let no one speak his name.
If anyone kills a guest at a hearth, let the master of the house pay the guest's price, because he guards the guest.
A guest is dear to the gods.

plan.english: Hear, kin of the slayer and kin of the dead man! I have heard the two houses. The slayer struck the dead man with a spear. So I decide: Let him pay a hundred cows and ten horses. Let the kin of the dead man take them, and let them not shed blood. Let both houses swear it by Sky. Whoever breaks this oath, let the gods punish him.

Let the kin of the dead man take them, and let them not shed blood.
Let both houses swear it by Sky.
Whoever breaks this oath, let the gods punish him.

plan.english: Whoever swears by Sky and lies, let him pay twice. Let no one trust that man. If a man promised a price and did not pay, let his kin pay it. Sky sees the oaths.

Let no one trust that man.
If a man promised a price and did not pay, let his kin pay it.
Sky sees the oaths.

title: Of the widow and the son

plan.english: If a dead man leaves a small son, let the widow hold the price. When the son has grown up, let him decide. If the widow does not take the price, let no one threaten her. Grief is not a trade.

plan.english: Husband, beloved, where are you? You went to the feast at evening. They carried you back at night. Your blood lies on my hands. Your hearth has grown cold. Your sons are small. I will not take their cattle. Weep, women!

title: Curse on the slayer of a husband

plan.english: Slayer of my husband, hear me! May your cows die in the field. May your sons not grow up. May your hearth grow cold. May sleep not come to you. May dogs and birds eat you. May the earth not take you.
